 Order
Applicant is in detention since 26.09.2024.
First application was dismissed on merits by the co-ordinate Bench vide order dated 10.01.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 55806/2024 and second application was dismissed as withdrawn.

2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that he alongwith co-accused harassed the deceased physically and mentally in relation to demand of dowry and after committing rape, she has been murdered by them therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36773 2 MCRC-22137-2025 against the applicant and co-accused.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
He is in custody since 26.09.2024.
It is further submitted that nothing has been seized from the applicant.
There is no eye witness or last seen witness in this case.
Applicant has been made accused only on the basis of memorandum of co- accused Sonu Arya.
It is submitted that FSL report does not support the prosecution case regarding present applicant.

It is submitted that after withdrawal of second application, court statements of PW-1, brother of deceased, PW-3,
mother of deceased, PW-3 father of deceased, PW-4 brother of deceased, PW-5 Suman Anuragi,
PW-6 Majju @ Majeed, PW-7 Heeralal Kori and PW-8 Sandeep Kumar have been recorded in which they have not supported the prosecution case regarding present applicant.

Charge sheet has been Anand Arya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6244955/
1 filed and trial will take considerable time to conclude.

sentences.text: Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as Objector have opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and prayed for its rejection.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:36773 3 MCRC-22137-2025 his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. Certified copy as per rules.
